title: Queensland seller disclosure documents
description: The documents a Queensland seller usually gathers for the seller disclosure statement (Form 2) and its prescribed certificates. Summarised from the Queensland Government's seller disclosure page; your conveyancer or solicitor confirms what applies to your sale.

sources.title: Buy, sell or lease a property with a pool

items.title: Engage a conveyancer or solicitor to prepare the disclosure statement
Get a current title search and the registered survey plan
List easements, covenants, leases and other encumbrances, including unregistered ones
items.detail: Your conveyancer checks registered encumbrances; tell them about informal arrangements you know of.

items.title: Have a copy of any residential tenancy or rooming accommodation agreement ready
Note the property's zoning under the planning scheme
Collect any notices you have received
items.detail: For example transport infrastructure or resumption notices, and notices or orders under the building, planning, QBCC and environmental protection laws.

items.title: Check the contaminated land and environmental management registers and any heritage listing
Find any tree application or order under the dividing fences and trees law
Note whether there is a pool on the lot or on common property, and find its pool safety certificate
For a body corporate lot, order the body corporate certificate and get the community management statement
Check and sign the disclosure statement (Form 2)
Give the statement and certificates to the buyer before they sign, and keep proof that you did
items.detail: At auction they must be given or made available before the fall of the hammer.

items.title: Tell your conveyancer if anything changes before contracts are signed
